subject: Greenline: Request for remedy credits + promotional trial extension
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@greenline.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: service interruptions earlier this week — request for credits and trial extension

Hi Soojin / Marissa,

Thanks for picking up earlier. To summarize: we had several 5–20s spikes and two ~3m interruptions across our api-redwood-us-west region between 2027-04-08 22:40 UTC and 2027-04-09 03:10 UTC. The incidents caused 18 failed prediction attempts for our fulfillment pipeline which forced a fallback to a slower rule-based path. That directly impacted 1,200 shipments across two shifts and a delayed SLA notification to customers.

We’ve filed an internal incident and logged impact; our finance team needs an accounting of credits for the affected usage and an extension on the trial window for a small portion of our pilot (we’re still in the 90-day evaluation period). Specifically we’re asking for:
- A goodwill credit to cover the failed prediction costs (approx $3,800)
- A 30-day extension of the trial period for the accounts in deal RL-2027-042

Can you confirm next steps and expected timeline? We’re trying to close an internal exec review and want to understand the remedy before that meeting.

Thanks,
Alex
VP Product, Greenline Logistics
ops@greenline.com
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@greenline.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2027 09:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: service interruptions earlier this week — request for credits and trial extension

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear summary and the patience. I’m sorry Greenline hit those spikes; that’s not the experience we aim to deliver.

Immediate steps from our side:
- I’ll open a formal remediation request with our SRE team for a timeline and root cause write-up (expected by EOD Monday).
- I’ll coordinate a provisional commercial gesture while we finalize the postmortem. My speaking with Marissa and Ben here.

Prelim offer (pending Ben’s confirmation): 15% usage credit for the affected billing period + a 30-day trial extension for the pilot accounts in RL-2027-042. If you prefer a token-set (one-time) top-up instead of percentage credit, we can do that as well — let me know which you prefer.

Will follow up shortly with the formal approval and a simple acceptance note you can reply to.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2027 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: service interruptions earlier this week — request for credits and trial extension

Ben — looping you in. Customer requests: ~ $3.8k apparent impact + 30d trial extension. Deal RL-2027-042 is still in pilot; we want to move them to committed capacity in Q3 but this exec review is blocking.

Questions for finance:
- Do we prefer percentage credit on the billing period or a one-time token/top-up?
- Is 15% acceptable as a standard gesture here or do we need manager signoff for anything >15%?
- If we go tokens, ballpark token equivalent of $3.8k (for record-keeping).

I’ve added the HubSpot ticket and the incident links here: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/67890

—Marissa
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: service interruptions earlier this week — request for credits and trial extension

Thanks for the context. I ran a quick calc and discussed with finance ops. Proposal:
- Approve a one-time token top-up equal to $3,500 to reconcile the failed calls (rounded down to avoid over-credit).
- Additionally approve a promotional package: 20k complimentary tokens + 30-day trial extension for the pilot accounts (RL-2027-042).
- No additional approvals required for this amount.

I’m attaching the credit calculation worksheet for audit: credit_calculation.xlsx (attached). Please make sure the HubSpot record notes the amount and that the tokens are allocated to the pilot account IDs listed in the ticket.

Ben Carter
Director, Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@greenline.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Final: remedy credits and 30-day extension for RL-2027-042

Hi Alex — thanks again for the detailed report and for working through this with us. Per our internal approvals here’s the final remedy package we can extend today:

1) One-time token credit of $3,500 applied to the pilot billing account to reconcile the failed calls.
2) Promotional top-up: 20,000 complimentary tokens applied to the pilot account.
3) Trial extension: 30 calendar days added to the accounts under deal RL-2027-042.

Acceptance steps: reply to this thread with a short acceptance line (e.g., \"Greenline accepts remedy package\") and we’ll schedule the token application and extension for the next business day.

References and next steps:
- HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/67890
- Incident postmortem will be shared by EOD Monday (I’ll drop the link here).

We’ve added a one-time promo code (GREENLINE-30EXT) for visibility in your billing UI. If you’d rather we place the tokens directly (recommended), let us know which pilot account IDs to credit and we’ll do the allocation.

Sincerely,
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com
